title: Genetics of Atropine for Myopia control in childrEn
summary: AIM (DRKS00023337), the parent study of GAME, is a randomised clinical trial (n = 300 participants) investigating whether high-dose atropine (0.01% and 0.02%) can reduce the progression of myopia in a Caucasian population of children, as previously shown for Asian children. Although the understanding of genetics in myopia has recently made considerable progress, it is still not known whether and to what extent genetic factors influence the efficacy of low-dose atropine therapy. Therefore, we plan to offer participants in the AIM study to determine their individual myopia risk score and correlate their genetic profile with the effectiveness of low-dose atropine therapy. This will help determine who will benefit from low-dose atropine therapy in the future and who will not (personalised medicine). We will offer to collect and store oral mucosal swabs from our patients once to have them ready for future analyses, possibly with external partners. The swab will be taken as part of a study visit for the AIM study.

interventions.name: One-time collection of oral mucosa swabs

criteria:
Inclusion criteria:
Participation in the AIM study, written informed consent obtained from the patient and his/her parents/legal guardians
Exclusion criteria:
No written informed consent
